The priest by the command of the law the right shoulder, etc., down to and Moses says in what follows.
8.29: 8.29 He took the breast. AUGUSTINE, question 23 on Leviticus. Above, because he commanded generally, etc., down to for from the beginning it is said: Be you to him in the things that pertain to the people, you to them in the things that pertain to God.
8.30: 8.30 And taking ointment. THE SAME, question 24. It is asked after the death of Moses who anointed the priest, etc., down to by obeying, not by excelling. He sprinkled, etc. Whatever goods are in us must be referred to him as to our head; hence: For them I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in truth. Openly therefore he called his passion sanctification, which sanctification is given to us. And upon the sons AUGUSTINE. It did not appear which of the sons succeeded the high priest. For Scripture does not define the firstborn or elder, unless in some divine judgment it was done, although it seems to have come from contention, that afterward there were several high priests, because when the more excellent contended, for the sake of ending the dispute the honor itself was granted to several.
8.31: 8.31 And the loaves also. He commanded the flesh to be eaten with the loaves, that we may understand the body of Christ, who is flesh, and the bread that came down from heaven, John 6., and this ought to be celebrated in the church only.
8.32: 8.32 Whatsoever remains. This we see done in the Church, and what remains unconsumed to be given to the fire. He does not say, however many days it remains unconsumed, that always, if it remain, it be given to the fire: hinting that if we fail in the eating of the sacrifice and cannot search whether what we see is the very body of the Lord, yet let us not leave it but give it to the fire, that the Holy Spirit may eat what we cannot. He eats however when we think possible to him what we cannot.
8.33: 8.33 From the door. It signifies that during the whole time of the present life one must not depart from the tabernacle, but persist in the service of God. AUGUSTINE, question 24 on Leviticus. At the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, etc., down to for habitation took this name. For seven, etc. ISICHIUS. The fiftieth, seven multiplied in itself, etc., down to observing the watches of the Lord, etc.
8.36: 8.36 And they did, etc. Aaron is joined to his sons, nor does he go out of the door of the tabernacle. For he was to be preached and in them to preach, as he himself consecrates and is consecrated in the members.
9.1: 9.1 On the eighth day, etc. The eighth day after the dedication signifies the day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit came, Acts 2. The seven days from the dedication hint seven times seven days, which were from the resurrection to Pentecost, namely 49, the day of Pentecost itself being added as an eighth. Pentecost, which fell on the day of the resurrection, bears the figure of the future, and of the consummation of the present age, because it revolves in seven days. For it was fitting that the Spirit come on the same day on which Christ rose. Then he says Aaron and his sons were called, and the elders: for then was convoked the spectacle of the Church, in which is Aaron, that is Christ, and his sons who are of high conduct, and therefore ministers of the priesthood, and the elders, that is the presbyters: of these the body of the Church consists.
9.2: 9.2 Take of, etc. Aaron takes a calf for a holocaust and a ram, and offers to the Lord. Then Christ made known his sacrifice when the Spirit coming gathered Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and the first-fruits of all nations into the upper room of the apostles, Acts 2. Aaron offers a calf and a ram when the doctors of the Church announce the mysteries of the passion and insinuate that they were celebrated for the salvation of the human race. Take. The apostles offered the he-goat on the day of Pentecost when Peter announcing penance said: Be converted and do penance. AUGUSTINE, question 26 on Leviticus. Take one he-goat of the goats, etc., down to but where all together, there also each, but is not converted.
9.6: 9.6 This is the word, etc. The word, namely, the thing commanded. Do this in commemoration of me, Luke 22. He says word, because more in the word is considered or consisted the dispensation of this mystery, and chiefly in the Lord's word transferring what appears into something greater and intelligible. Hence of the manna also he says: This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat, this is the word which the Lord has commanded, Exodus 16. In these therefore he signifies that the holy mystery, they acting and celebrating the Lord's supper, the Holy Spirit came. For it was the Lord's day on which it was fitting for the apostles to celebrate the sacred mysteries: whose traditions we following assign the Lord's day to divine assemblies. Likewise we find Christ manifest after the resurrection through the mystic supper and the breaking of bread.
9.7: 9.7 And offer for sin, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 27 on Leviticus. Another reading, etc., down to it is not necessary to be laid upon the holocaust. Offer the holocaust, etc. He does not say holocaust of consummation, as above, when it was offered that by sanctification he might be consummated, to perform the priesthood, which he was performing. It is to be noted that when sacrifices are offered for the people, sacrifices for sin are commanded to be offered, and holocaust and sacrifice of salvation. For the priest it was offered for sin and the holocaust of consummation, not of salvation. But the consummation was offered when the priests were sanctified. And these Moses offered for Aaron and his sons, but afterward Aaron already performing the priesthood is commanded to offer for himself a calf for sin, and a ram for a holocaust not of consummation; for then it was offered that by sanctification he might be consummated, and be able to perform the priesthood, which when he was performing, it was not necessary to consummate again.
9.8: 9.8 And immediately, etc. ISICHIUS. For what cause these sacrifices are also performed here we said above, etc., down to hence in the person of the priest we see both offered. AUGUSTINE, as above. It also moves that when Aaron made the gifts of the people which are mentioned above, etc., down to each from each living creature, as if he said breasts.
9.15: 9.15 And for sin, etc. ISICHIUS. Whose figure these have, etc., down to and they ceased not to meditate what would teach the Church. Stretching forth his hand, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 28 on Leviticus. Standing at the altar he served, etc., down to who forbade steps to be there.
9.22: 9.22 And thus finished and the rest. ISICHIUS. He evidently wishes to expound the whole figure of the Church, etc., down to the following show.
9.23: 9.23 And Moses and Aaron going into the tabernacle of the testimony, etc. THE SAME. Because of the intelligible tabernacle, etc., down to he is fit to give the blessing. And going in. He premised going in, and adds coming out, because the priest enters the tabernacle when he prays for himself or for the people, or is at leisure for divine contemplation; he comes out when he teaches, or blesses the people, or when he returns to conscience searching himself lest perhaps he offend in preaching. And the glory of the Lord appeared. In the appearance of fire, as on the day of Pentecost, hence he adds: And fire came forth from the Lord. Hence Luke too: There appeared to them parted tongues as of fire. To all the multitude, etc. To which Luke says the like: And when this voice was made, the multitude came together, and was confounded in mind, Acts 2.; not only came together but was afraid. Hence here it follows: And they were astonished and wondered, etc. Which were upon the altar. He found that it is necessary to lay the aforesaid sacrifices and their expositions upon the intelligible altar of the body of Christ, that our intention may sigh thither, and then the nourishments of the intelligible fire, that is of the Holy Spirit, will be present, of whom it is said: Our God is a consuming fire, Deuteronomy 4.
10.1: 10.1 And Nadab. AUGUSTINE, question 31 on Leviticus, vol. 3. The fire coming out from the Lord the sons of Aaron died, etc., down to they shall suffer torments. And taking, etc. ISIDORE, questions on Leviticus, vol. 5. They offer strange fire, etc., down to lest we burn with vices. ISICHIUS. Here those who teach strange things, etc., down to whence they could merit life. AUGUSTINE, as above. Another reading, etc., down to through whom he gave us Scripture.
10.4: 10.4 And calling Mishael and Elzaphan. Mishael, touching of God. Elzaphan, or Elzaphan, illumination of God, or mirror of God. To these it is rightly commanded to carry Nadab and Abihu out of the camp. For these signify the saints, who, illumined by God, touch him with the hands of faith, and contemplate God with perfect faith. Hence well are they called sons of Uzziel, which signifies the Gospel: hence he is said to have been Aaron's cousin, because great is the kinship of the Gospel and the Law. For the Gospel is the exposition of the Law: and the sons of the Gospel thrust out the truly dead heretics from the camp of the Church. Or Misadai and Elzaphan the first the touching of God, that is Misadai; Elzaphan is interpreted watchtower of my God. Whoever knows how to touch God, and to behold Christ, the flesh namely and divinity, like Thomas who, touching the flesh with the hand, said: My Lord and my God, John 20., can take away the fire of strange doctrine from the face of the saints, that is of the priests. The tunics of the priests, the conduct and life by which they are clothed with the habit of the priesthood. They are cast away therefore with the priesthood from the fellowship of the priests and also of the people. Hence he adds, outside the tabernacle, that is the church of the people, the sons of the paternal uncle of Aaron do this. Aaron, that is David, by whom the prophecies are understood, which make Christ manifest, and in a way bring forth to the ignorant. The brother of prophecy is the Gospel; for what was done in the Gospels was foretold by the prophets. The sons therefore of the brother of the father Aaron, that is of the Gospel, eject such. Hence: If any come to you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into the house, 2 John.
10.6: 10.6 The heads, etc. According to the letter. Because they had lately been consecrated to God, he commands that they not lay aside the holy vestments, but stand by ready to serve God. Allegorically, however, that they make no division of persons in Christ. For the head of Christ is God, but Christ consists of divinity and humanity; the tiara of the head, that is of the divinity, is the humanity, with which the divinity was covered as with a cap; this is not to be taken away, nor division of persons in Christ preached, but one person of two substances. Your heads, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 32 on Leviticus. Lest, namely, they lay aside the cidaris, etc., down to hence he adds: Your brethren and all the house of Israel shall bewail the burning. ISICHIUS. We are not ignorant what the cidaris signify, etc., down to of which: His anointing teaches you of all things.
10.9: 10.9 Wine and anything that may inebriate. THE SAME. Up to now the Church keeps this law, etc., down to that is spiritually inspired. Wine and anything, etc. They are commanded to abstain from what casts down or overthrows the state of mind, when they enter the tabernacle. But let us never be drunk, but always sober in mind and body. When you shall enter. AUGUSTINE, question 33. When then was it lawful for them to drink, etc., down to that this be the lawful office of the priests forever in their generations.
10.10: 10.10 That you may have knowledge to discern. AUGUSTINE. This also is placed ambiguously, etc., down to or rather is it to be referred to both?
10.12: 10.12 Take the sacrifice, etc. ISICHIUS. That the breast confidence, etc., down to but what pertains to the peace and salutary offerings belongs to the whole people. Take, etc. The secrets, namely, and deep mysteries of Scripture which the crowd cannot grasp are to be retained and eaten by the perfect; beside the altar, that is beside the faith and authority of the Lord's passion.
10.14: 10.14 The breast, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 34. The breast. Although names have been given to each, etc., down to from the breast was laid on the altar.
10.16: 10.16 Meanwhile. ISICHIUS. Because every sin is blotted out by penance, and those who committed the aforesaid sin of another doctrine and blasphemy were not saved, the lawgiver expounds the cause of their death. Meanwhile the he-goat, namely because the sons of Aaron did not eat what was for sin in the holy place, that is, they did not make the penance of the sin committed to be performed in the church. To whom this command is given, whom Christ has appointed in the Church as his vicars. For he himself offered the blood of his oblation, which was offered for our blood, into the holy, that is into heaven, in the sight of the Father. This sacrifice ought to be eaten in the holy place, that is the church, for the propitiation of sins, hence he adds: As it was commanded me, that is as I commanded. For Moses bears the person of Christ. He found it burnt, because they had sinned against the Holy Spirit, the offering for penance was taken away by the intelligible fire of the Holy Spirit. For to those sinning willfully there remains no sacrifice for sin, Hebrews 10. For as true penance merits pardon, so feigned penance provokes God: for the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, Wisdom 1. The holy Fathers called this the irremissible sin and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, to persevere in crimes to the end of life, to despair of one's salvation, to distrust the power and mercy of the Redeemer. ADAMANTIUS. Not to sin belongs to God alone, etc., down to unless true and sincere. AUGUSTINE, question 36 on Leviticus. Since six animals are commanded to be offered for the people, etc., down to all which had been for sin.
10.19: 10.19 Aaron answered, etc. In the person of the Church, whose figure he bears, as also of Christ, Aaron seems to say this. As if, because after the coming of the Savior they were deputed to minister, and to offer for penance, and to expound the prophetic life. Otherwise: The teachers perished and in them these things befell the Church, that she bewail the death of priests and masters, hence she could not today eat for sin, nor pray: but it displeased the Lord. AUGUSTINE. Aaron answered, etc. If today they offered what is for their sin, etc., down to But why this was done, Aaron answered, and it pleased Moses. Today. As if to say: if before the remission of the Savior they had so sinned, perhaps it would be pardoned, when knowledge was not yet manifested to the world: hence, If I had not come, and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin, John 15.
11.1: 11.1 The Lord spoke. ISICHIUS. Whatever is made by God is clean by the very authority of the institution. In animals therefore the morals of men are painted, and acts, and wills, from which they become clean or unclean. THE SAME. The Lord said to Noah: Everything that moves and lives shall be meat for you, Genesis 9., etc. In Genesis also it is said: God saw all things that he had made, and they were very good, Genesis 1. Here, however, some are forbidden as evil, and decreed unclean. Yet these are not contrary to each other: for the Lord briefly restrains the gluttony of the Jews, and the spiritual exposition of the precepts instructs what they ought to be. For the law is nourishment of the rational soul rationally understood. As above through the offerings he figured the offerers, so now through what is eaten he expresses the eaters.
11.3: 11.3 Everything that has, etc. ISIDORE. In fishes whatever has not fins and scales is abominable: rough things are counted for clean. For bristly and hairy, firm and grave morals of men are approved. Those without them are called unclean, to whom light and slippery, weak and effeminate morals are added. He also joins fins and scales; for whatever fishes are finned and scaly. If to some ignorance is soluble, to these also sublime knowledge and heavenly life: but those who are not such, with these not even to take food. Morally. GREGORY. Fishes that have fins and scales are wont to leap over the waters. In finned fishes therefore the elect souls are figured, which alone pass into the body of the heavenly Church; which, supported by the fins of virtues, leap through heavenly desire to contemplation, although they fall back into themselves through the fragility of the flesh. They alone pass into the body of the elect as choice food, who, while they serve the lowest things, climb to heavenly things by leaps of mind, lest they always lie hid in the depths of cares, where they have no care of the highest love, as of free air. Those therefore who are occupied with temporal things then dispose outward things well when they anxiously take refuge in the inward, nor love the noise of disturbance, but rest in themselves within in the bosom of tranquility.
11.10: 11.10 Whatsoever fins, etc. There are also fishes having a shell in place of skin, whose scale cannot be taken off, because neither by the word of God do they lay aside the scales of ignorance, nor receive the knife of the spirit: and though they are found in the sea of baptism, or in the rivers of penance, yet they are abominable in those things which move and live in the waters, because the regeneration and life which they received in baptism they corrupt by living ill.
11.11: 11.11 Flesh. RABANUS on Leviticus. When he forbids the swine, etc., down to seeking the darkness of night.
11.13: 11.13 These are of the fowls, etc. ISICHIUS. What pertains to the life of the contemplative he adds, etc., down to little women laden with sins.
11.14: 11.14 The vulture according to its kind. THE SAME. Who delights in wars. Hence follows the army, expecting the corpses of the dead: he ought not to feed on another's mourning who gives himself to contemplation.
11.16: 11.16 The ostrich. The ostrich is a bird, but cannot fly, and is always about the earth, like some who serve God and entangle themselves in secular business, Job 39; 2 Timothy 2. The owl. They say this sees sharply by night and little by day. Such are those who glory in the contemplation of the Law, and cannot take in the light of the Gospel. The night raven. It plunders only by night. Such are the nations gaping after the works of the night, which are fornication, uncleanness, impudicity, Galatians 5. The gull. The gull is an animal dwelling in water as on land: for it flies and swims. To this are likened those who venerate circumcision and baptism. The hawk. The hawk is among the birds of prey, but grows tame, and does its plunder with men. This is imitated by those who seem meek but strive to plunder with the powerful and covetous and rapacious. The cormorant and the ibis. These have long necks, and as is said draw food from the depth of earth or water, nor are they to be imitated. For he who is at leisure for contemplation ought to tend to higher things, nor be anxious about lower.
11.19: 11.19 The hoopoe. This is mournful and loving mourning. The sorrow of the world works death. But he who loves God ought to rejoice, pray without ceasing, in all things give thanks, 1 Thessalonians 5. The bat. Which flies about the earth, uses wings for feet: which is foreign to those who contemplate, lest their contemplation be occupied with earthly things.
11.20: 11.20 Every thing of fowls that goes upon four feet, etc. Those who seem like the contemplative, but like creeping things cling to earthly concupiscences, even if they walk on four feet, that is if they pretend the evangelical preaching which calls to penance; because they do not truly embrace the social life, serving pleasures, are abominable.
11.21: 11.21 But whatever goes, etc. Because though they are in the flesh, they do not walk according to the flesh, 2 Corinthians 10., but leap from filthy actions, and are mingled with earthly men, to instruct and teach: as the Lord with sinners and publicans, Matthew 9. We ought to have legs higher than feet, lest we halt on both feet, as the Jews in the law and the prophets; but let us have straight legs, like the Cherubim, of whom it is said: Their legs were straight, and their feet winged, Ezekiel 1.
11.22: 11.22 The bruchus. Which leaps, but less than the attacus or locust, which leap more. Such are those who converse with sinners, for conversion, not for consent or imitation. The ophiomachus. Who fights with serpents, but our fight is with the ancient serpent and his angels, Apocalypse 12.
11.25: 11.25 That he may carry. As he who calls evil good, and bitter sweet, Isaiah 5.: for by praising the evil which he ought to have forbidden, he makes it his own and carries it.
11.26: 11.26 Every beast which. ISICHIUS. The law passes over no sin; whatever are forbidden in the Gospel are expressed in the enigmas of the Law, that in the mouth of two witnesses every word may stand, Matthew 18., and in both laws you may praise God, and, as he forbids, flee evil.
11.27: 11.27 That which goes upon hands, etc. He who migrates the evangelical conversation, but walks on hands, for the sake of base gain, namely, laying on hands, 1 Timothy 4., he is rightly compared to all beasts, so that you may call him adulterer, or covetous, murderer and the like: for he communicates in all by the wicked laying on of hands.
11.28: 11.28 He that shall carry such carcasses. By giving false testimony, calling the unworthy worthy, and the clean unclean.
11.29: 11.29 The weasel. Gluttony. For the mouse avoids no dangers for the gluttony of its belly. The crocodile. Which, of hard skin and malicious, feeds on mud.
11.30: 11.30 The chameleon. It shows pity, and for weakness feigns itself gentle, when it is cruel. The mole. A blind animal born of the earth. For it is created, they say, of rained-on and muddy earth, but first corrupt.
11.31: 11.31 He that shall touch, etc. If they were naturally unclean, he would be unclean who touched even the living. The carcasses of such are actions, that is guile, theft, duplicity, and the like, in which is death of the soul.
11.32: 11.32 And upon what, etc. ISICHIUS. The lawgiver uses an admirable division, etc., down to both wooden vessel and garment.
11.34: 11.34 All meat, etc. By meat and drink he understands good works, therefore he said: The meat that you shall eat, and the liquid that is drunk, etc. Because both food and drink of evil actions are forbidden, that no one partake. If therefore on good actions, which are in every vessel, that is in every man, any carcass fall, necessarily the action will be unclean. For if on a good action pride, guile, hypocrisy or any carcass, that is bringing death to the one partaking, fall, this too will be unclean: for an evil intention falling on a good action pollutes it. If water be poured upon it. AUGUSTINE, question 37 on Leviticus. Of the vessel, namely, which was made unclean from unclean carcasses if perhaps it had water. Water. Of baptism: for the discourse is of the baptized; of unbelievers he makes no mention. Hence Paul: I wrote to you not to mingle with fornicators, 1 Corinthians 3., not certainly the fornicators of this world, etc.
11.35: 11.35 Or ovens. By this are designated teachers, in whom the foods of sacred doctrine are cooked by the operation and fire of the Holy Spirit. Nor is it wonderful: Moab is called a cauldron: Moab the pot of my hope, Romans 2. Chytropodes, etc. Because those who teach not to steal, steal; and those who preach not to commit adultery, commit adultery: yet the doctrine is clean. Hence fountains and the rest.
11.37: 11.37 If it fall. ISICHIUS. He leaves nothing unexamined, etc., down to if any carcass fall upon them, they become unclean.
11.39: 11.39 He that shall touch the carcass thereof shall be unclean. ISICHIUS. We ought to abominate the life of the wicked, to imitate that of the just. For he who touches the life of the wicked shall be unclean until he repents.
11.40: 11.40 He that shall eat. That is, as an advocate defended, and in helping transferred to himself, let him wash his garments, that is wicked actions, until he repent.
11.41: 11.41 Every thing that creeps upon the earth. This the lawgiver expounded above, but to the frequent meditation of the law, admonishing the hearer, he repeats.
11.47: 11.47 And that you may know what to eat. These foods do not cleanse or pollute us, but we ourselves: for we give life to what is eaten, and as every food is good, 1 Peter 2., and nothing is to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving; so what is eaten, that is what nourishes the soul, good actions namely, we give life to, if we use them well: if ill, we put them to death. For he who makes alms from robbery puts it to death, and takes away its power; and those who abstain from foods, but detract from their brethren, put abstinence to death.
12.2: 12.2 If a woman, having received seed. ISIDORE, questions on Leviticus, vol. 5. The week is the present life, etc., down to nor in the future will be purified. She shall be unclean. ISICHIUS. Because, namely, the sower is unclean, as heir of Adam, who by transgression was unclean, and thus mixed with his wife. For after he went out of paradise he knew his wife, and so the human race is propagated. Seven days. THE SAME. Because Adam, etc., down to when Adam, separated from paradise, fell into this misery. On the eighth day, etc. THE SAME. The eighth day, etc., down to But disobedience contracted uncleanness and filth for us.
12.4: 12.4 Thirty-three days, etc. THE SAME. Seven being added, etc., down to for it is uncertain whether they bear a female or a male. AUGUSTINE, question 40 on Leviticus. What difference is there between seven days, etc., down to in a female eighty. She shall touch nothing holy. What does he mean to understand by sanctuary, since none but priests ought to enter the tabernacle, and up to the second veil: beyond the veil, however, where the ark was, the high priest alone entered? Perhaps before the tabernacle, where the altar of sacrifices is, it could be called a sanctuary. For often the court also is called a holy place, when it is said: In the holy place they shall eat them. Thither perhaps women entered offering their gifts, to lay on the altar.
12.6: 12.6 And when the days are fulfilled. He opens the intention, because, namely, natural motions do not make pollution, but sin, of which David says: Behold I was conceived in iniquities, Psalm 50., etc., calling nature mother, and signifying that the uncleanness of the sin of Adam and Eve descended on the whole human race. Therefore Moses, the days of purification fulfilled, commanded a holocaust and a sacrifice for sin to be immolated; plainly showing that the image of God gives perfection to our race. For the days of cleansing show the formation, the holocaust the perfection. AUGUSTINE, as above. Is it a sin to have borne? etc., down to not that they might say for a son or daughter, but for a son or daughter. It is to be noted how poor the Lord willed to be born, that for him there should be offered not a lamb and a young pigeon or turtledove, but a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons according to the Gospel, which the Scripture of Leviticus then commanded to be offered if the hand of the offerer had not a lamb, which is great enough. BEDE, on Leviticus, vol. 2. Our Lord not only man, etc., down to and afterward to the heavenly Jerusalem, commended to the Lord by the victims of good works, she shall come.
12.7: 12.7 From the issue, etc. As if someone asked: whence shall she be cleansed who has lawfully begotten? he says, from the issue of her blood, that is disobedience, whence uncleanness and punishment flowed, by meditation and contemplation of the law, the neglect of which brought uncleanness upon men.
13.1: 13.1 And the Lord spoke. ISIDORE. God speaks once, and two are heard: Moses hears the Spirit, as the higher; Aaron the letter, as the lower, who announces the letter to the people. Hence he himself shall speak to the people, and shall be your mouth, but you shall be to him in the things that pertain to God, Exodus 4.
13.2: 13.2 A man. THE SAME. Sometimes it is taken excellently, he who keeps the image of God and the dignity of nature. Sometimes the sinner, in whom the dignity is deformed, as here. In whose flesh, etc. He bears leprosy in flesh and skin who strives to persuade carnal or outward things, like the Corinthians, who thought the resurrection to come would be in the pleasure of the flesh: and that sins are not imputed to those remaining in the faith, however carnally they live. Or as shining. Leprosy, one excessively or moderately dark, the passion not yet boiling over, which needs great deliberation. Another very clear and distinct, whose knowledge is open. The plague of leprosy. ISIDORE. Leprosy is false doctrine; lepers are heretics, who, not having the unity of the true faith, profess various errors of doctrine, mixing true with false and, like leprosy on bodies, by spreading defile the Church. He bears leprosy in the body who detracts from the Church, like the Carpocratians, who deny the resurrection of the flesh, and the Novatians, who condemn marriage and take away penance from sinners. Or to any one of his sons, etc. Of kinsmen according to the spirit, from whom he has the priesthood, in whom is perfect and full prophecy, that they may be able to discern subtle things and the hidden motions of the soul.
13.3: 13.3 Hairs. Thoughts, by which the soul is adorned, and the mind covered, by which they are begotten, as the head begets hairs, by which it is adorned and covered. Hence the very hairs of your head are all numbered, Matthew 10. Hence the Nazarites do not cut the head, Numbers 6., because they have not superfluous thoughts, but to put away holy ones is loss. Lower than the rest of the flesh, etc. Lower than himself: hence rightly he does not deserve pardon. To be conquered by another greater is bearable; but not to work the good commanded by God, for the Lord divides as he wills, that anyone become worse than himself, this is unbearable.
13.4: 13.4 He shall shut him up. He is shut up a second time, that he may be studiously examined, and the double trial past, strict judgment be made. The sin was manifest to the priest, but he did not know whether the mind consented to the passion, but conjectured: therefore he inspected again. Hence the Lord after the denial asks a third time how Peter's mind stands, John 11., that we may not judge quickly, but inquire frequently. He is shut up seven days. The number seven signifies the fullness of the present life, which is spent in seven days, which being fulfilled, sin and servitude shall cease. Hence the seventh in the divine Scriptures is named rest.
13.6: 13.6 He shall cleanse him, because it is a scab. So Paul removed from the tabernacle of the saints the man who in Corinth committed fornication because the passion was manifest, and delivered him to Satan; whom when he inspected a second time and saw him repent, he ordered him received, 1 Corinthians 5.
13.10: 13.10 And if the color in the skin be white. A manifest transgression of the letter of the law, which is proper to the Jews, as in sacrifices and purifications and the like. For there is also a common one for the Gentiles, of adultery, robbery, avarice, and the like.
13.12: 13.12 But if it break out. ISICHIUS. He shows the Jewish people partly leprous, as in part a transgressor of the law: hence the priest expels him as unclean. But the Gentile leprous all over the body, who transgresses the whole law, he does not expel; but judges him clean, because he was not subject to the yoke of the law. JEROME. But if it break out, etc. In this leprosy as it were flourishing and white, he designates diverse crimes. Because when the pleasure of worldly life is counted as it were white and flourishing, then the grave contagion of vices rages in the body. For either the spots of avarice or of lust show themselves. But the crime of avarice can easily be cut off, hence: Give alms and all things are clean to you. Lust also is cleansed by fasting and abstinence. But to all a remedy is applied through the priest. For one is cleansed by offerings of sacrifices; another is that which is more easily; another that which, placed outside the camp, is cleansed; another that is not cleansed at all.
13.14: 13.14 The living flesh, etc. ISICHIUS. The Jewish commandment, which is said to live as to the commandment, or because well understood it brings life.
13.18: 13.18 For the flesh, etc. ISIDORE. In living flesh he bears leprosy who thinks something false of the soul, which is the life of the flesh. Like the Luciferians who say the soul is propagated from the substance of the flesh; and the Arabians who think the soul dies with the body.
13.19: 13.19 A scar, etc. THE SAME. In the scar of a healed wound they bear leprosy who, after the knowledge of the faith and the medicine of God which they receive in Christ, again show some indication of error or of the perfidy of the old dogma. White. Because from the wound of legal transgression; for the law is white and not warmed by the sun of justice, Acts 15. Reddish. Because from evangelical transgression, as to eat what is offered to idols, blood, or the strangled; each is done against Christ, whose are the Law and the Gospel.
13.20: 13.20 He shall contaminate. Because sin is in the habit, and an evil devouring of the soul has settled through the ulcer. Hence he called leprosy breaking out from a wound. The flesh and skin which fire had burnt, etc. ISICHIUS. He seems to repeat the foregoing, but partly says the same, partly adds, for he puts another passion but the same indication. For he dealt with the ulcer which is generated and grows from some sickness of neglected flesh. The ulcer of our flesh is therefore pleasure, drunkenness, gluttony and the like, which arise from a luxuriating body itching within itself. But now of the greater plague, that is burning by fire. Of which it is said: Fire shall consume the adversaries, Isaiah 74.
13.25: 13.25 Because the plague, etc. In the scar of burning the Manichees have leprosy, who in the torment of abstinence burn their bodies, and through unbelief beget thence not cleanness but leprosy.
13.29: 13.29 A man or woman. Who, namely, errs about the divinity, like the heretics who not only deny the Father maker of the world but also affirm him author of evils, like Manichaeus. Or beard, etc. ISIDORE. In the beard they bear leprosy who think perversely of the apostles and disciples of Christ, and contrive to preach falsehoods. For the beard is the ornament of a man, and the apostles are the teachers of the body of Christ. ISICHIUS. Six kinds of leprosy we find the lawgiver has put, etc., down to because they defend the perfidy of their error with open depravity. THE SAME. He supposes diverse colors of leprosy, etc., down to signifies a lying tongue and weakness.
13.31: 13.31 He shall shut him up seven days, and on the day, etc., not so much for punishment as for the sake of strict probation; for time is to be kept in all things, more strictly in those whose tongue is unbridled about the divinity.
13.34: 13.34 If on the seventh day. Because the word in which one offends, if he who sinned once denies it, ought not to be judged. For who judges a guilty man for what the tongue confessed, if he denies he uttered it voluntarily? And his garments washed he shall be clean, etc. JEROME. Others committed before baptism, etc., down to of which it is said: He that sins against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, etc.
13.37: 13.37 Black hairs, that is, if he has shone with his impiety, and done true penance. For mourners and penitents are disfigured with black dress.
13.38: 13.38 A man or woman, etc. ISICHIUS. In the transgression of divine dogma, etc., down to by which they may not live.
13.40: 13.40 He is bald and clean. Simple, not foolish; for there is no one to whom at least a few hairs do not remain.
13.44: 13.44 Whosoever therefore is defiled, etc. ISIDORE. Heretics are cast out from the Church until they are purged. With rent garments, that is, their secrets made manifest, they are commanded to sit. With head bare, that their nakedness may be seen by all. With mouth closed, lest they speak impious things any further.
13.46: 13.46 He shall dwell outside the camp. So John excludes the intelligible leper from the intelligible habitation: He that brings not this doctrine, receive him not into the house, and say not to him, God speed you, 2 John 10. ISICHIUS. These things are ridiculous interpreted according to the letter, etc., down to lest it be said to him, You who preach not to steal, steal; but to the sinner God said: Why do you declare my justices? Romans 2.
13.47: 13.47 A woolen garment, etc. THE SAME. Woolen, precious and warming the mind, etc., down to namely also good works.
13.48: 13.48 In the warp, etc. JEROME. The warp is the soul: which when by the spindle of temptation it is twisted into thinness of threads, is bound with the solidity of firmer virtue. The soul stands, therefore, as though erect, the sense of the body is subject like the weft; but some are sins of the body, others of the soul. ISICHIUS. Those who attend only to the letter, etc., down to but also of that which is wont to happen about virtues. THE SAME. Leprosy in a linen garment, etc., down to in the conversation of this life. Skin or whatever, etc. THE SAME. The temptation of tribulation, etc., down to nor as clean rashly receive.
13.49: 13.49 If white, etc. THE SAME. Septuagint: Greenish and yellowish, that is pride, which flourishes for a little: hence, As the green herbs they shall quickly fall away, Psalm 36., or vainglory. For Christ wills virtues to be without vainglory.
13.56: 13.56 He shall break it off. By penance he shall cut off the passion; pride is broken off by applying humility; vainglory by removing flattery and vain praise.
13.57: 13.57 A flying leprosy. GREGORY, hom. X on Ezekiel. Sometimes we know that we have done evil things and avoid them, etc., down to by immoderate continence passes to the vice of anger.
14.1: 14.1 And the Lord spoke. ISICHIUS. Because the spots, etc., down to for he himself healed every sin.
14.4: 14.4 Two sparrows. THE SAME. The divinity, namely, and humanity of Christ. Clean, because he had no sin; and living, because from sin he was not liable to death. Which to eat, etc. Because the Word was made flesh, and unless we eat the flesh of the Son of man, we shall not have life in us. Cedar wood. ISICHIUS. The cross, which is strong against all, as the cedar is strong and incorruptible. Scarlet. Septuagint: twisted scarlet the passion, namely, because scarlet is red, twisted with passibility and impassibility interwoven. Hyssop. The grace of the Holy Spirit, which cooperates with our cleansing. Hence: You shall sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed, etc., Psalm 50.
14.5: 14.5 Over the waters, etc. Of baptism. Whoever of us are baptized in Christ, are baptized in his death, Romans 6.
14.6: 14.6 He shall dip in the blood, etc. Because all are comprehended in the power of baptism. The living sparrow is dipped in the blood of the killed sparrow, because we are baptized not in the passion of man only, but of God and man.
14.7: 14.7 Seven times that he may be rightly purified. For the sevenfold Spirit, in whom is all cleansing and remission; or that the soul be purified from seven demons. And he shall let the sparrow go. Because in a way it is held under the contemplation of human understanding.
14.8: 14.8 His garments. Works and whatever virtues he has had, because sin pollutes these also. And being purified, truly. Above, however, it was said that the leprosy is cleansed, but it is thus to be understood, fit to be cleansed. Outside the tabernacle. The fellowship of the saints, from which sinners are excluded. Hence with such a one not even to take food, 1 Corinthians 5.
14.9: 14.9 The hairs. The thoughts which give adornment to man as rational and discussing many things, like the hairs of the head. And the eyebrows. Which make the contemplative man of sublime and more divine things, which the eyebrows set in higher parts signify. Of the whole body. Even of the shameful parts, that none of the old thoughts remain, that wholly new and as if newly born he may put off the old man, put on the new. For as with hairs shaved new ones succeed, so if new thoughts sprout toward better things, the old being shaved off.
14.10: 14.10 On the eighth day. On which the Lord rose, on which the leper enters the camp, which the patriarch Jacob saw, angels meeting him: hence he called the place the camp of God, Genesis 32. After. On the first day, on which the priest goes out, he commanded a sacrifice to be immolated outside the camp for the uncleansing of the leper, on the eighth day he substituted other sacrifices. These have the same force as the first: because all time is ended in weeks. The eighth therefore is the first that follows. And it is to be noted that he shows leprosy, that is sin, to be most carefully avoided, in that he commanded it to be purged so diligently. Lambs without blemish, etc. All these figure the sacrifice of the Savior, who was the victim for us. The sacrifice is made of both sexes, because he saved both sexes. JEROME. In the two lambs the two comings of Christ, in which we must believe that we are cleansed from the leprosy of sins, for first he came and suffered: the second time he is to come in glory. A yearling. He commands the sacrifice to be a yearling as perfect: for in the aforesaid animals yearlings are perfect: hence they are then fit for generation. And three tenths. For he who is cleansed by the sacrifice of the Only-begotten ought to be signed with the faith of the holy Trinity, three tenths of fine flour, that is the Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit having in each person perfection: for ten is perfect. Fine flour. Of the Only-begotten. For though it was the passion of the Only-begotten, yet it is the work of the whole Trinity: hence we are baptized in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, while we are baptized into the death of Christ. ISIDORE. There is leprosy of sin, etc., down to and to obtain pardon. A sextarius of oil. Because by faith each of the aforesaid is understood and done. A sextarius is a measure, holding neither more nor less: for what is more is poured out, if less it is not a sextarius. So faith is given to the measure of our mind, and holds neither more nor less than is distributed by God: for what is more or less is outside faith. A sextarius of oil, the fat mercy of God and grace: and if it could not bear forth the brightest face of holiness, let it not extinguish the lamp of faith.
14.14: 14.14 On the tip. That he may fortify the hearing and make it cautious: lest it hear the voice of the serpent any more. And of the foot. That in the sight of God our motion and way be directed. For these things aforesaid being kept by the blood of the lamb and his faith, which is given us by his mercy and compassion, the intelligible leprosy is put to flight.
14.16: 14.16 And shall sprinkle, etc. For such a priest is confident with God, because he has been able to cleanse and forgive sins: hence he sprinkles seven times, because the number is of remission and grace.
14.17: 14.17 And what, etc. That the faith of the priest be shown in works. For he does not otherwise exert his force unless the hand is taken, that is the action confirmed and signed. He puts oil in the left hand, and dips the right finger in oil, that by the arms of justice on the right and left he may move about, through glory and ignobility, through infamy and good report.
14.19: 14.19 And he shall offer sacrifice, etc. By what has been said about offenses, those which are for sin can be conjectured: for they are neighbors and common as in common matter. Holocaust, etc. The sacrifice of Christ first cleanses us from offenses and sins, and then our holocaust is made. For when by intelligible cleansing we have been made spiritual, sanctifying body and soul, then we are made worthy of the ascent of the altar: for then we receive full cleansing, nor need any other. For there are advances of cleansings, for one frees from the pollution of leprosy; another brings into the camp; another presents the most fully cleansed to the altar.
14.20: 14.20 He shall put upon the tip of the right ear of him who, etc. ORIGEN, hom. 8 on Leviticus. You see how of the last and highest purification, etc., down to and in all things the Son of the Father is repaired.
14.21: 14.21 But if he be poor and his hand cannot, etc. JEROME. That is, if he has not the riches of heavenly charisms, for instance, if he could not keep virginity, let him keep the marriage bed undefiled; if he could not carry off the trophy of martyrdom, let him at least keep himself unconquered. But if he be poor, etc. Wonderfully he condescends and, granting pardon to poverty, commands sacrifices fit for the poor, lest he be dismayed if sacrifices beyond his strength are required. But who has not bread or money to buy a lamb or dove or turtledove? To spiritual things therefore we are called by occasion of these, that we may understand leprosy as malice; penance as cleansing. The works of penance are necessary which can blot out sins. Hence: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of penance, Luke 3. There are however many who cannot pay what the strictness of penance demands. For it demands constant prayer, alms, vigils, holy fasting, and that he may be able to say: My tears have been my bread day and night; and, I will wash my bed every night, I will water my couch with my tears, etc., Psalm 14. And, For I did eat ashes like bread, etc., Psalm 101. He forgives those who are willing but unable another way of penance, that is, seeks other kinds of sacrifices.
14.34: 14.34 Canaan. ISICHIUS. The land of the Canaanites was promised to Abraham, etc., down to which is evident there: Salute Nympha, and the church that is in her house, Colossians 4.
14.40: 14.40 Outside the city. Not only outside the house, because they are to be cast out from the universal Church, which is the city of the living God.
14.42: 14.42 And other stones. The dogmas of truth, of which it is said: The holy stones are rolled over the land, Zechariah 9.; and elsewhere: Whoever shall build upon the foundation gold and silver, etc., 1 Corinthians 3.
14.44: 14.44 The leprosy returned and the walls, etc. That is, if, the wicked dogmas being cast out, by subtle exposition again the doctrine of impiety is found sprinkled.
14.48: 14.48 But if the priest going in, etc. Remember what you have read in the cleansing of the leper. For it plainly appears that it expresses the church of the heretics; which acts against the dispensation of the incarnation of Christ: and therefore for cleansing the house he adds such sacrifices in which the mysteries of the flesh and passion of Christ can be expressed, and sins committed against them healed.
14.54: 14.54 This is the law. Because he expounded widely the laws of leprosy, he necessarily recapitulated, first the genus, then the parts he expounds. Of leprosy. Of impious doctrine, which befalls laity also, therefore it is added: Man or woman in whom the plague of leprosy is and goes. For if he had understood priests only, he would not have added woman. After this he put the leprosy that is in virtues, for these are the garments of the soul. Then that which is in the teachers of the Church, who are the walls of the house. At length he makes mention of the scar and breaking out of pustules: describing true leprosy, namely that which is in sins either doubtful or manifest.
15.1: 15.1 ISICHIUS. The Septuagint thus, etc., down to into a perfect man, etc.
15.2: 15.2 GREGORY, book XXXIII of Morals, ch. 15, vol. 2. The man who suffers, etc. What is speech but seed? etc., down to than the fruit of perpetual reward. ISICHIUS. Because there are many kinds of wicked doctrine, etc., down to if he has been partaker of his doctrine following his disciples.
15.9: 15.9 The saddle on which, etc. ISICHIUS. Septuagint, that is, the covering of the ass. By which a more negligent disciple and soft of heart to be changed is understood. For saddles are soft.
15.13: 15.13 He shall number seven days. THE SAME. Because through the sevenfold Spirit remission of sins is given, whose seven gifts those need who are to be perfectly cleansed.
15.14: 15.14 Two turtledoves. THE SAME. A sacrifice worthy of teachers. The turtledove indeed designates meditation, the dove, frequently begetting and simple, the Holy Spirit. For a teacher must beget spiritually: worthily therefore he dedicated this sacrifice to priests and masters.
15.15: 15.15 Before the Lord that he may be cleansed. According to the will and law of God, for what he sinned he is cleansed by repenting, by offering sacrifices of prayers, and henceforth by living rightly and perfectly understanding.
15.16: 15.16 The man from whom, etc. ISICHIUS. Unless someone, etc., down to cleansed the human race. THE SAME. Because many, etc., down to by the traditions of their teachers.
15.17: 15.17 The garment and skin. It expresses the misery of original sin, by which the human race, defiled, defiled even the senseless. It expresses women who for lust are mingled with men for the temporal use which they furnish, and the garment, the skins too grown old, are cast away, and the womanly custom, friendship growing old, is rejected.
15.19: 15.19 A woman, etc. By the menses wicked thoughts are designated. For she who suffers the menses does not touch another's flesh and defiles herself. So wicked thoughts and wills, although not fulfilled in work, are held and punished with God as deeds. The woman who returning. ISICHIUS. He attends both to women, etc., down to which is the corruption of the human race. Seven days, etc. It signifies the universality of times, up to the fulfilment by which the Gospel was declared: for men were separated from God until the evangelical preaching joined them. He that shall touch his garment shall wash, etc. So we must abstain from idolatry: that we touch neither idolaters nor their disciples or favorers, whose beds or vessels as it were they use, nor have communion with them.
15.25: 15.25 The woman who, etc. Because we have said that the one suffering a flow of seed teaches obscene and corrupting things; and uses Jewish doctrine whence the seed of coition goes out; there remain those who spread the doctrine of the Gentiles, which is opportunely called a flow of blood, as the seduction of idolatry: for demons rejoice in blood.
15.29: 15.29 She shall offer. Above he commanded the one suffering a flow of blood to take two turtledoves or pigeons for a sacrifice, because she occupied the place of a master; and here too the one who suffers a flow of blood because he too was master of idolatry.
15.31: 15.31 You shall teach. This he sanctioned neither of lepers nor of those who touch carcasses. Uncleannesses. Every sin is uncleanness of the soul, but idolatry most of all. Tabernacle. The inner man, in whom is the image of God. The Word also was made flesh, and dwelt among us.
15.32: 15.32 These. Those things which cohere with each other and have a common intent he is wont to join, to show how they ought to be understood, and which are joined with which in kinship of sense. And he who, etc. He who teaches Jewish precepts, and teaches good things badly, is unclean, while he brings forth what pertains to the letter out of season, as he uses clean things as unclean, hence: To the clean all things are clean, etc. And she who, etc. These are they who teach impiety, since the human race was held by the error of idolatry in menses, that is in the separation of malice.
16.1: 16.1 And the Lord spoke, etc. ISICHIUS. He makes one body of the law, etc., down to hence after their death the Lord speaks this to Moses.
16.2: 16.2 Speak to Aaron, etc. THE SAME. How much God spares us, etc., down to which is guarded against by present words. Before the propitiatory. ISICHIUS. Septuagint: Before the face of the propitiatory, etc., down to or which we receive from the flesh of the Lord.
16.3: 16.3 He shall offer a calf for sin. ISICHIUS. A wonderful order. For when he had said that we should not always enter the holies, lest we presume to approach rashly and incautiously, he shows when and how we should enter. He shall offer a calf for sin. The beginning of the divine preaching is Christ, and his passion, if this had not been, and he had not freed men from error, Gentile as well as Jewish, he could not speak of the divinity of the Father. For no one knows the Father but the Son and he to whom the Son will reveal him, Matthew 11.
16.4: 16.4 He shall be clothed with a linen tunic, etc. He who is about to speak of God, and to see him as far as possible, let him be armed with all virtues, of which four are general, justice, chastity, fortitude, wisdom. The breeches. JEROME, letter to Fabiola, vol. 1. Where it is related how Moses clothed Aaron his brother, etc., down to we shall die the death. THE SAME. According to the Hebrews, etc., down to therefore with linen breeches the woman or thighs are covered. When he is washed. ISICHIUS. The water of baptism, etc., down to but desiring to understand the dispensation of Christ.
16.5: 16.5 And he shall receive from the whole multitude, etc. THE SAME. Christ was immolated for us, etc., down to hence Paul: You are made dead by the body of Christ, Romans 8.
16.7: 16.7 Two goats, etc. ISICHIUS. Because both for sinners and for the just, etc., down to saying: You shall have no strange gods, Exodus 20. AUGUSTINE, question 55 on Leviticus, vol. 3. Two goats, the goat to be immolated, etc., down to the allegorical signification. ISICHIUS. He shall make the two goats stand. Because Christ God and man, etc., down to and the other the scapegoat Christ.
16.10: 16.10 Into the wilderness. That is, into the bosom of the Father, where no one comes but himself and the Holy Spirit. He departed, therefore, that is, held back the power of working, and bore our iniquities, not to have them, but to consume them. For God is a consuming fire. Into the wilderness, of which it is said: In a desert land, and where there is no way and no water, etc., Psalm 62. There the enemy has no place, where God abides. For the divinity is said at the time of the passion to have gone away into heaven; not changing place, but in a way holding back power, that the wicked might consummate the passion.
16.11: 16.11 The calf. When Christ is offered for the deliverance of the Jewish people, he is called a calf: because he observed the justification of the law. Hence he says: I came not to destroy the law but to fulfill it, Matthew 5.; who was made of a woman, that he might redeem those who were under the law, Galatians 4. Rightly therefore he is called a calf, as subjected to the commandments of the law. ISICHIUS. That the sacrifice of Christ is indeed of the flesh by the power of the divinity, and in the good pleasure of the Father, and a propitiation for our sins: and is performed for the ministration of the spirit, the lawgiver makes manifest.
16.12: 16.12 Of the coals of the altar, etc. With spiritual words, which John wrote at the supper after Judas went out, in which he expounds how he himself, being in the Father and the Father in him, sends the Spirit; how the Father is the husbandman, he the vine, the apostles the branches, and many other things which kindle to piety like coals of fire, John 18. Taking with his hand. 70. He shall fill his hands with incense, of subtle composition, praying subtle, namely, spiritual things, not earthly. The incense is prayer. Hence: Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight. For Christ prayed for the disciples.
16.13: 16.13 That being put, etc. Aaron, according to the dignity of the priesthood, signifies Christ and other priests. Christ places upon the fire, that is doctrine, the spices, that is prayer; and the vapor of the cloud, that is the power of prayer, covers the oracle, that is the flesh, from which to us is propitiation of sins in Christ, who is also the testimony. Every priest too, speaking of Christ, places in the fire of spiritual doctrine the spices of prayer, whose power covers the oracle, which is over the testimony, nor suffers him to inquire about the passion of Christ, things beyond the power of the inquirer, and he shall not die by immoderate questions, namely. And he shall not die. His flesh saw not corruption, because it was covered with the vapor of the spices, with the power, namely, of prayer, of which it is said: You will not give your holy one to see corruption, Psalm 15.
16.14: 16.14 Against the propitiation. Because for our propitiation and illumination Christ suffered, who is called the propitiatory, and the east. Hence: Behold the man, the East, etc., Psalm 15. And elsewhere: and the East visited us, etc., Zechariah 6. Or against the propitiatory, that is, in the sight of the Father, seven times, because he gave us remission of sins and the Holy Spirit.
16.15: 16.15 And when they shall have slain, etc. Because Christ was made of the common mass of men, he is rightly called a goat, because this animal is rough and hairy with hair, and for sin the human race. Hence fittingly he says: And when he shall have slain the goat for the sin of the people, Hosea 1., that is of the human race: which once was not a people, now however a people, since Christ took its first-fruits. To show therefore that he bears the first-fruits chiefly of the Jews, but also of all nature that is in sin, he took a calf and a goat together, and because there is one sacrifice and one effect, necessarily common things are done in the goat and the calf. For you see that the goat is killed before God, that is the Father: and the blood is carried into the inner parts of the veil, that is to the same Father. And the sanctuary is expiated, the mass, namely, of the human race, which from the beginning was holy, and a tabernacle of the Holy Spirit.
16.16: 16.16 The tabernacle of the testimony, etc. What above he called the sanctuary, here he calls the tabernacle of the testimony. For for the same reason the mass of the human race is called both holy and tabernacle of the testimony. For as the tabernacle of the testimony is heaven, it is rightly called holy: our man is heavenly, of whom Paul says: As we have borne the image of the earthly, etc., 1 Corinthians 15. He is rightly called holy who is in the midst of uncleannesses, because Christ is assailed by the passions of the flesh. Sanctuary. The human race, taking flesh, that in the proper sanctuary of the flesh he might pray by the cross.
16.17: 16.17 Till he come out. Giving up the spirit, namely, in the human way, and leaving the flesh in the sepulchre.
16.18: 16.18 And taking the blood. Because by his passion he sanctified the horns of the altar, that is the four principal virtues.
16.19: 16.19 He shall expiate. By the sacrifice of Christ they are expiated. Hence, the heavenly things themselves are expiated by better victims than these, Hebrews 2. From uncleannesses. As to the powers of heaven they need not be expiated, which are in perpetual sanctification. But because the smoke of our sins frequently ascends, of which it is said: There went up a smoke in his wrath, Psalm 17.; and of Nineveh, Its malice is come up before me, Jonah 1., he rightly expiates the supernal choirs from our uncleannesses, to take away the abominable odor. Therefore he sprinkles not simply but seven times, because by the pardon of our sins the heavenly things are cleansed.
16.20: 16.20 After. AMBROSE, letter to Simplicianus. As there are two in the field, etc., down to which make tranquility of mind.
16.21: 16.21 And both hands laid, etc. The laying on of hands ministers blessing in the sacrifice, or remission of sins, or the Holy Spirit; which cannot be in him on whom falls the lot of the devil. Many circumstances also contradict that opinion. And laid. To show that the Word of God impassible, immortal, in the flesh took on a sufficient sacrifice for us: on him rightly all sins are laid, because he bore our sins in his body. Septuagint: He shall lay them upon the head of the living kid. In which is signified the crown of thorns pressed on his head, for in thorns sins are signified. By a man, etc. Christ who is all, of his own sacrifice priest, sacrifice, worship, and altar. Ready according to that: But I do not gainsay, I have not gone back: I have given my body to the strikers, etc., Isaiah 50. Christ therefore, immolating himself through the living kid, himself sends, through the ready man, that is his own power, the living goat into the wilderness, the immortal, namely, and impassible divinity, to places impassable to us and deserted of all malice. Hence: Jesus knowing that the Father had given him all things into his hands, and that he came from God and goes to God, John 13. ORIGEN in his homily on Leviticus says that the goat which is immolated to the Lord signifies those who are destined to the lot of the Lord, as that Lazarus who is carried by angels into Abraham's bosom, Luke 16. The goat, however, that is sent into the wilderness signifies the reprobate, or the Jewish people, who are cast away from the face of the Lord for their sins, like the rich man in purple buried in hell. The ready man, Christ or his angels, whence each receives what he deserves.
16.26: 16.26 And he that shall let go. ORIGEN, hom. 9 on Leviticus. Has concupiscence ascended into your heart? etc., down to and here in washing the garments the same figure can be preserved.
16.29: 16.29 And in the seventh month. ORIGEN, as above. In which is the solemnity of repropitiation, etc., down to that is cast out and refused.
17.1: 17.1 And he spoke, etc. By the present law it is shown that the Lord speaks not to Moses only, but to all in common. He desires all to know what is expedient for all, that the law is temporal, and, its time being fulfilled, is observed superfluously. The fulfillment of the time is perfect, the destruction of the place in which he commanded sacrifices to be offered, intimating that he who sacrifices outside the camp, or outside only the tabernacle of the testimony, shall perish from his people, that, namely, the tabernacle and place being destroyed, the sacrifices may have an end. But holy actions, and those which build up the human mind, as to honor father and mother, and love neighbors, and the like, he did not circumscribe by place, because they always profit and agree with the Gospel. Whoever therefore now act the figures of the destroyed place, shed blood, and defile the common conversation, sin in common; as those who shed blood shed also the blood of those whom by their example they send into error.
17.3: 17.3 Any man, etc. As if the figures of the law are temporal, and in a certain place, which being destroyed they cannot remain. If he kill a sheep. AUGUSTINE, question 56 on Leviticus. He does not speak of these, etc., down to whatever he did in this matter could not be against the law, because he is the giver of the law.
17.7: 17.7 And no more shall they offer their sacrifices to devils, etc. Since it was said by the Lord, Exodus 20.: You shall not make to yourself a graven thing, nor the likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or in the earth beneath, nor of those things that are under the earth; they made a molten calf, and offered it sacrifice, desiring to lick up the sacrifice. The law therefore, as their pedagogue, commands to sacrifice to God, Exodus 32., that, occupied in this, they might abstain from the sacrifice of idolatry. Such sacrifices, however, it sanctioned by which future mysteries are signified. With which they have committed fornication. He calls idolatry fornication, because God espoused our souls to himself. Fornication then is called departure from him. He terrifies also those who fornicate in the flesh, when he compares the sin of fornication to the worship of idols and the offering to demons.
17.8: 17.8 A man of the house of Israel, etc. AUGUSTINE, as above. If the same command is repeated, etc., down to they vainly boast themselves Israelites or Jews.
17.10: 17.10 Of the strangers. The Gentiles, who are not joined to the Jews, but with us. For with them we have been, having their law and the prophets and the promised inheritance, yet cleaving not to them but to God: therefore according to the Septuagint he said man man, to show that both those in circumcision and those in uncircumcision who cleave to God ought to keep this commandment. If he eat blood, etc. By blood we understand murder; hatred of a brother is murder: For he that hates his brother is a murderer, 1 John 3. One must abstain therefore from all hatred of brethren, because upon such a soul that eats such blood according to that: Who devour my people as they eat bread, Psalm 13. God sets his face, Christ, namely, who is the image of the Father. For he that sees the Son sees the Father also, John 14. For he is the judge, of whom it is said: But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth, Psalm 33. He destroys the one eating blood from his people, from the common kind of men, namely: because as the unmerciful and impious he sends with the malignant spirits into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels, Matthew 25. To show how merciful to each other we ought to be, how loving, he shows that for our expiation he shed his own blood, saying: I have given it to you, the blood namely of Christ.
17.11: 17.11 The life of the flesh. AUGUSTINE, question 57 on Leviticus. There is something vital in the blood, etc., down to for whom he acquired so great merit.
17.13: 17.13 Any man whosoever. ISICHIUS. God has great care of us that we harm not one another: therefore to him that strikes the cheek he commands to give the other; and to him that takes away the cloak, to let go the coat also; and not to contend in judgment, lest from contention we wish even to harm, Matthew 5., but by suffering to correct him. Therefore the lawgiver recapitulates the command about blood, to take away varied frauds and cunning of harming, saying: Whether by hunting or fowling, etc. By hunting. By fraud, which pertains to blood and life. Hence: They hunted after the soul of the just, and condemned innocent blood, Psalm 43. And again: Our soul as a sparrow has been delivered out of the snare of the fowlers, Psalm 123. That is, if he sees the sinner who is exposed to hunting and guile through weakness or simplicity. Or sheep, etc. He, namely, who removes himself from earthly things, which it is lawful to eat: for the violent and covetous eat such. Hence: If you bite and devour one another, take heed you be not consumed one of another, Galatians 5. Or since before they were just, rightly they are counted among the clean. Let earth cover it, etc. The earth covers the sins of the confessing, as remaining below and mortified by penance: whose cry is forbidden to ascend to heaven, whither ascended the cry of Sodom, who would not do penance, Genesis 18.
17.15: 17.15 The soul that shall eat, etc. Above it was said: Who shall touch carcasses taken by beasts, that is who shall communicate in such: here, however, it is said: The soul that shall eat; that is made the whole sin his own, and from it fulfilled his will.
18.2: 18.2 I am the Lord. As if to say, Know your creator; diligently keep his precepts.
18.3: 18.3 According to the custom, etc. He opens the intention of the whole law, that we abstain from evils and hold to good. Neither in their laws, etc. For not only from fornication, avarice and pride, but also from divinations, and auguries, and the superstitions of all nations he commands to abstain.
18.5: 18.5 He shall live in them. I am the Lord. Because in them is true life for those believing in Christ: because he who sees the Son and believes in him has eternal life, John 6. This he did not add in the earlier judgments and precepts: for the law does not give life unless the gospel supervene.
18.6: 18.6 Every man to her that is near, etc. He forbids that we cunningly approach sinners in the law on the occasion of kinship, that at last, knowing their foul deeds, we betray them; hence he adds: I am the Lord. Every man. Septuagint: A man shall not approach to any domestic of his flesh, etc. For as man is twofold, so the precepts are twofold, teaching the inner and the outer man. The outer law forbids mixing with blood relations, like the Gentiles, whose inheritance Israel was to receive, who so dissolute and given to the pleasures of the flesh that one took many wives, that so at least they might abstain from foreigners. The lawgiver therefore follows out the generations in order, from whom they ought to abstain, lest the generations be confounded and the inheritances perish. The union of such he calls turpitude, to show it abominable and horrible. And it is to be noted that when at the beginning of this law he had said: I am the Lord your God, he repeated I am the Lord, signifying that he is joined to us in the flesh, and a partaker of our kinship: to offend so great a kinship is damnable. I am the Lord. Not manifesting the sins of men, but blotting out and covering what has been blotted out or uncovered by confession. Turpitude, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 58 on Leviticus. He forbids to lie with the mother, etc., down to for in charity he sins, which is the fullness of the law, Romans 13.
18.9: 18.9 Born abroad. THE SAME, question 59. From the mother, if by a former husband, etc., down to which above he said obscurely.
18.11: 18.11 The daughter of your wife, etc. AUGUSTINE, as above. Not with the daughter of the stepmother by a former husband does he seem to forbid intercourse, since she is not a sister to him to whom it is forbidden, either by father or by mother, he added: by the same father.
18.14: 18.14 The nakedness of your father's brother, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 61. It is asked whether this, etc., down to for someone could think that it was lawful for him to marry such a one and not fear adultery. Nor shall you approach, etc. Septuagint: And to his wife you shall not go in. For this they call the nakedness of the father's brother, that is of the uncle, the private parts, namely, of his wife.
18.16: 18.16 The nakedness of your brother's wife, etc. In the mother concupiscence, in the daughter action is understood, in the granddaughter death. For concupiscence conceives sin, sin death, James 1., or another sin; as David from concupiscence committed adultery, and for adultery killed.
18.17: 18.17 That you may reveal her shame. As though sin were familiar and akin to us. Hence we ought to compassionate one another, and bear our burdens, that we may fulfill the law of Christ, who bore our sins.
18.18: 18.18 The sister of your wife, etc. AUGUSTINE, questions on Leviticus. He does not forbid, etc., down to lest he make her commit adultery. You shall not take to concubinage nor reveal, etc. Septuagint: To her jealousy, as if this were jealousy between sisters, as if it were not also between those who are not sisters. Or rather lest this be done with the intent that a sister be brought in over a sister for jealousy? In peace God has called us, let us have peace with all, Romans 12., especially with neighbors. In Jewish conversation also it is not fitting to take up the ecclesiastical, nor celebrate the typical Passover with the true, nor circumcision with baptism. Hence Paul: If you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing, Galatians 5. The Jewish conversation, mortified, ought to be joined to the Church, which is the sister of the law, and has the same teachers, the same prophets. But the Jewish conversation is jealous, because its riches have passed to the Church. Hence Paul says: They are zealous for you not well, but would exclude you, etc., Galatians 4. For the first wife is jealous, because the second comes in. Hence Leah says: Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband from me? Genesis 30.
18.19: 18.19 To a woman, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 64 on Leviticus. When he had sufficiently forbidden this above, etc., down to but it is forbidden as harmful to the offspring to be conceived.
18.20: 18.20 With the wife, etc. ISICHIUS. Here adultery is forbidden again, which is also forbidden in the Decalogue: whence it appears that those were so forbidden that even their husbands being dead they should not take wives, whose nakedness he forbids to be uncovered.
18.21: 18.21 Of your seed, etc. THE SAME. Fittingly these are subjoined, etc., down to nor are we mixed in the error of the Gentiles. Nor shall you pollute, etc. Not only by luxury, or sacrificing to idols, but also by introducing the philosophy of the Gentiles into the Church. For what consent has the temple of God with idols?
18.23: 18.23 A woman shall not, etc. Not only for men, but also for women is the law set, 2 Corinthians 9. Hence: Who shall find a valiant woman? Proverbs 13. For as the male signifies a strong and constant soul in virtues, so the woman designates one keeping her dignity: for she was made a help to man, Genesis 2.: she who is such ought not to be stained by intercourse with beasts.
18.24: 18.24 Neither be you defiled in any of these things, etc. ISICHIUS. How great the pollution is in the aforesaid the punishment of the polluted shows. Nor is it to be carelessly passed over that what are joined to one another he collects into one, to show that he who has been polluted in one offends in all, James 2. All nations are defiled, etc. The demons, who on account of their multitude are called all nations. Who, though they rejoice in every sin, yet chiefly in fornication and idolatry, because in these both body and soul are stained, and the whole man, who is called earth. But God visited the earth, that is the race of men.
18.29: 18.29 Every soul, etc. For those who after the evangelical preaching commit such things find no other medicine for the evil; nor shall they be in the lot of men, but of demons.
18.30: 18.30 Keep my commandments. As if: The commandments are mine, not man's; to whose image you are made; which you ought not to defile: because you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you, 1 Corinthians 3.
19.1: 19.1 The Lord spoke... Be holy. ORIGEN, hom. 12 on Leviticus. What this name holy means, etc., down to that namely in the world you may have conversation.
19.3: 19.3 Every one. He builds upon a foundation: as if, be holy, that the Holy One may dwell in you; and bestow the kindness of nature by honoring father and mother. Keep my sabbaths. ISICHIUS. Wishing to recapitulate the commandments of the law, that is, You shall not kill, You shall not steal, etc., etc., he says: Keep my sabbaths. For the true sabbath is to cease from all evil. Hence Moses: You shall do no servile work in it, Exodus 31. Keep my sabbaths. God, wishing to teach us of the intelligible rest, and of the consummation of the world, when it is impossible to prepare food or work, or be occupied about anything bodily, says through Moses: Sabbaths today to the Lord, you shall not find it in the field, Exodus 16., etc. Note that he does not say sabbath, but sabbaths, because the intelligible rest is quiet and free not from one but from all carnal things: therefore in this place first the name of sabbaths is put in divine Scripture, that you may know that the sabbath is full and perfect rest.
